messages:
alex: Noticed a burst of NVMe controller resets and multipath path losses in eu-west1 around 04:12 UTC. GPU attach queue climbed to ~70 and some attaches timed out.

maria: Ugh. Paging @sandeep @jen for storage/attach triage. Any signs this is host-local or over fabric?

sandeep: Checking logs now. Initial dmesg shows `pci link down` on nvme-of endpoints and `nvme-controller reset` loops. Looks like link-level instability.

alex: paste from one host:

```
[04:12:05] nvme nvme1: controller reset (status 0x1)
[04:12:06] nvme1n1: I/O 1 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[04:12:06] nvme-multipath: path lost /dev/nvme1n1
[04:12:06] pci 0000:5e:00.0: link down
```

jen: Also see a big spike in janitor/ephemeral-cleaner runs at same time window. Cleaner churn could amplify IO retries.

kai: Are these NVMe-oF targets over RoCE? If so microbursts can look like PCI link flaps.

sandeep: Confirmed: hosts in these racks attach NVMe-oF over RoCE to local storage appliances. Network team: any fabric events?

network-dev: We observed a short east-west congestion spike at 04:12 UTC in eu-west1 affecting RoCE priority lanes; opened INF-8942. Likely packet drops causing controller timeouts.

ops-bot: infra-bot: INF-8942 created: eu-west1 RoCE lane congestion (04:12 UTC).

maria: Immediate mitigations we should do now: 1) throttle ephemeral janitor concurrency in eu-west1; 2) add temporary backoff on attach-controller and increase attach timeout; 3) avoid scheduling large GPU batches to affected racks. Thoughts?

sandeep: +1. I'll push a temporary autoscaler rule to avoid packing large jobs onto those racks and increase attach timeout to 90s.

jen: I'll prepare a safe canary to throttle janitor to 15% concurrency in eu-west1: `opsctl set infra.janitor.concurrent_fraction=0.15 --region eu-west1 --canary 10` — starting canary in 2 mins.

alex: Canary started. Also moved 30 pending GPU pods to fallback pool manually which brought attach backlogs down to single digits.

lucy: Noted a small uptick in customer job retry billing for that window. Finance FYI: there may be a transient cost blip due to reattempted attaches.

kai: Confirming no kernel nvme driver flips during incident. Please avoid kernel-level tuning until we have postmortem signals.

network-dev: Fabric metrics look stable again at 04:25 UTC after a micro-config roll and buffer tuning. Will follow up in INF-8942 with root cause and remediation.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: eu-west1 janitor throttle canary (10 hosts) succeeded. Global rollout scheduled for 5m if no regression.

jen: Postmortem action items draft: - Implement janitor rate-limit per-region with automatic backoff on fabric/error signals. - Add attach-controller exponential backoff + extended timeout. - Add multipathd nvme path-loss SLI and alert when path-loss rate > threshold. - Consider RoCE QoS adjustment for NVMe lanes.

sandeep: I'll collect NVMe/oF traces, multipathd logs, and attach-controller metrics and drop into the incident binder. Thanks all for quick coord.

alex: TL;DR: RoCE microburst caused NVMe-oF controller resets -> multipath path loss -> GPU attach queue spike. Mitigations: janitor throttle, attach timeout/backoff, move pods off racks. Monitoring to validate.
